title: October 17, 2017
overview: Activate’s Tech and Media Outlook 2018 by Activate Activate’s third annual Tech and Media Outlook examines consumer trends, technology innovations, and industry dynamics expected to shape technology and media businesses in 2018. It presents forecasts and analysis on revenues, consumer media use, smart speakers, reality computing, web video, premium video, sports, news, eCommerce, and podcasting, drawing on proprietary research and large-scale U.S. surveys. A 2018 report on technology and media trends, including consumer internet and media revenues, digital assistants, VR/AR, web video, premium video, sports, news, eCommerce, and podcasting. It covers global and U.S. markets where specified, with forecasts including 2017–2021.
methods: Activate-labeled forecasts estimate global consumer internet and media revenues for 2017E–2021E; cited inputs include eMarketer, GroupM, IBISWorld, IFPI, the International Monetary Fund, NewZoo, PricewaterhouseCoopers, RBC, the World Bank, and ZenithOptimedia.

The report cites the Activate 2017 Consumer Tech & Media Research Study, with chart-specific sample sizes including n=4,047, n=2,406, and n=996; platform-specific samples are also reported (Facebook n=2,641; Snapchat n=969; YouTube n=2,940).
Top news sites were selected from comScore’s Top 100 digital news properties; figures cover desktop and mobile sites only.

Virtual Pay TV churn covers the trailing twelve months beginning September 2017, while SVOD churn covers calendar year 2016. key_findings: Activate forecasts that global Internet access revenue will contribute $128B of consumer Internet and media revenue growth at a 5.7% CAGR over 2017E–2021E.
Activate forecasts that global paid-content revenue will contribute $108B of consumer Internet and media revenue growth at a 4.7% CAGR over 2017E–2021E.
Activate forecasts that global advertising revenue will contribute $66B of consumer Internet and media revenue growth at a 2.3% CAGR over 2017E–2021E.
For U.S. adults age 18+, average daily time spent with technology and media is forecast to increase from 12:28 in 2017E to 12:46 in 2021E.

The report identifies platform portability as a potential game changer: Google Assistant and Alexa are accessible to third-party developers and OEMs, who have integrated and distributed the assistants across a wide range of devices.
Activate forecasts global consumer and enterprise spending on VR/AR will reach $71B in 2021E.
limitations: Top news sites are selected from comScore’s Top 100 digital news properties; figures cover desktop and mobile sites only.
Virtual Pay TV churn covers the trailing 12 months beginning September 2017, while SVOD churn covers calendar year 2016.

Virtual Pay TV programming-cost analysis averages base offerings across major services and includes only services offering broadcast networks and/or sports programming; estimates include a premium for reduced scale and its impact on per-channel costs.
The smart-speaker timeline uses either product announcement or launch date.

sections.section_label: There are 31 Hours in a Day
sections.summary: This section considers how consumers divide time across technology and media and forecasts further growth in daily engagement. Its forecast describes an increase in average daily time spent with technology and media by 2021.
key_points: Daily Hours Spent per Adult (Age 18+), U.S., 2017E–2021E: average daily time with tech and media is forecast to rise from 12:28 in 2017E to 12:46 in 2021E (p. 10).
The report identifies smart speakers as a driver of audio listening and, for devices with screens, video consumption; self-driving cars are identified as enabling more multitasking (p. 10).

sections.section_label: Super Users: A Lot More Time, a Lot More Money
sections.summary: The section distinguishes high-engagement video users from other users and compares their share of video time with their share of consumer spending. It presents these “Super Users” as a disproportionately valuable audience.

sections.section_label: Smart Speaker Battles are about the Great Digital Assistant Wars
sections.summary: This section frames smart speakers as an entry point in a wider contest to own digital assistants and their conversational interfaces. It forecasts rapid adoption but also argues that standalone speaker sales will face limits as assistants spread across dev...
key_points: Share of Smart Speaker Owners, U.S., 2017: 17% of consumers own a smart speaker; Amazon Echo and Echo Dot are the largest displayed device categories (p. 27).
Smart Speaker Unit Sales, U.S., 2016–2021E: forecast sales rise from 8M units in 2016 to a peak of 41M in 2019E, then decline to 31M in 2021E (p. 21).
The report describes dedicated speakers as a “trojan horse” for bringing AI into the home and forecasts that digital assistants will become ubiquitous across a broader set of devices (p. 22).
